title: Read: katakana extras
description: Voiced sounds, combined sounds and more. Learn the basic characters first.

units.title: G sounds
intro: Katakana takes the same two marks (dakuten) as hiragana. Put them on the K row for the G row: ga, gi, gu, ge, go.
The shapes do not change, only the marks are added: カ becomes ガ, キ becomes ギ.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ga'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'gi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'gu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ge'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'go'.

units.title: Z sounds
intro: Two marks on the S row give the Z row: za, ji, zu, ze, zo.
Same surprises as hiragana: シ becomes ジ (ji) and ス becomes ズ (zu).
ヂ and ヅ exist but are rare, so we skip them.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'za'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ji'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'zu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ze'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'zo'.

units.title: D sounds
intro: The T row with two marks gives the D row. Only three are common: da, de, do.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'da'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'de'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'do'.

units.title: B sounds
intro: The H row with two marks gives the B row: ba, bi, bu, be, bo.
These are very common in loanwords: bus, building, button.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'ba'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'be'.
Same shape as the plain character, with two small marks at the top right: 'bo'.

units.title: P sounds
intro: The H row with a small circle gives the P row: pa, pi, pu, pe, po.
Two marks means B, a circle means P.

items.hint: Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pa'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pi'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pu'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'pe'.
Same shape as the plain character, with a small circle at the top right: 'po'.

units.title: Combined sounds: キャ, ギャ
intro: Just as in hiragana, a small ャ, ュ or ョ blends with the character before it. キ and ャ make キャ (kya).
The small character is half size and sits low and to the right. kya is one beat, not two.

items.hint: キ plus a small ャ: say 'kya' as one sound, one beat.
キ plus a small ュ: say 'kyu' as one sound, one beat.
キ plus a small ョ: say 'kyo' as one sound, one beat.
ギ plus a small ャ: say 'gya' as one sound, one beat.
ギ plus a small ュ: say 'gyu' as one sound, one beat.
ギ plus a small ョ: say 'gyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: シャ, ジャ
intro: With シ and ジ the i drops away: シャ is sha and ジャ is ja.
So the pattern is sha, shu, sho and ja, ju, jo.

items.hint: シ plus a small ャ: say 'sha' as one sound, one beat.
シ plus a small ュ: say 'shu' as one sound, one beat.
シ plus a small ョ: say 'sho' as one sound, one beat.
ジ plus a small ャ: say 'ja' as one sound, one beat.
ジ plus a small ュ: say 'ju' as one sound, one beat.
ジ plus a small ョ: say 'jo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: チャ, ニャ
intro: チ and ニ combine too: チャ is cha, ニャ is nya.
ニュ in ニュース (news) is one you will see often.

items.hint: チ plus a small ャ: say 'cha' as one sound, one beat.
チ plus a small ュ: say 'chu' as one sound, one beat.
チ plus a small ョ: say 'cho' as one sound, one beat.
ニ plus a small ャ: say 'nya' as one sound, one beat.
ニ plus a small ュ: say 'nyu' as one sound, one beat.
ニ plus a small ョ: say 'nyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: ヒャ, ミャ
intro: ヒ and ミ combine: ヒャ is hya, ミャ is mya. These are rare in loanwords.

items.hint: ヒ plus a small ャ: say 'hya' as one sound, one beat.
ヒ plus a small ュ: say 'hyu' as one sound, one beat.
ヒ plus a small ョ: say 'hyo' as one sound, one beat.
ミ plus a small ャ: say 'mya' as one sound, one beat.
ミ plus a small ュ: say 'myu' as one sound, one beat.
ミ plus a small ョ: say 'myo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: リャ, ビャ
intro: リ and ビ combine: リャ is rya, ビャ is bya.

items.hint: リ plus a small ャ: say 'rya' as one sound, one beat.
リ plus a small ュ: say 'ryu' as one sound, one beat.
リ plus a small ョ: say 'ryo' as one sound, one beat.
ビ plus a small ャ: say 'bya' as one sound, one beat.
ビ plus a small ュ: say 'byu' as one sound, one beat.
ビ plus a small ョ: say 'byo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Combined sounds: ピャ
intro: The last ones: ピャ, ピュ, ピョ (pya, pyu, pyo). They are rare. ピュア (pure) is one example.

items.hint: ピ plus a small ャ: say 'pya' as one sound, one beat.
ピ plus a small ュ: say 'pyu' as one sound, one beat.
ピ plus a small ョ: say 'pyo' as one sound, one beat.

units.title: Small ッ
intro: A small ッ means: pause briefly, then say the next consonant twice. カット is 'kat-to', with a held beat in the middle.
You do not pronounce ッ by itself. It is silence, one beat long.
It is half the size of ツ and sits low on the line.

items.meaning: a short pause: the next consonant is doubled
items.hint: Looks like ツ but half the size and low on the line. Say nothing: hold the next consonant a beat longer.

units.title: The long mark ー
intro: In katakana, a long vowel is written with a bar: ー. コーヒー is ko-o-hi-i, with two beats on each long sound.
The bar always points along the writing direction: it is a horizontal line in horizontal text.
Do not confuse ー with the kanji 一 (one). The long mark only ever follows a katakana character.

items.hint: A plain horizontal bar after a character. Hold the vowel of the character before it for one extra beat.
